title: New Hypertrophy Gimmick™ just dropped 🤡
summary: NH critiques the low-rep (4-6/4-8, 'anything above 8 is junk volume') hypertrophy method popularized by Paul Carter. He grants that low reps suit heavy compounds and weighted calisthenics and can reduce fatigue, but argues narrow low rep ranges stall progression on isolation lifts, fail with rest-pause, push people toward machines only, and amount to a softer repackaging of Mentzer's HIT. He works across 3-15 reps and returns to YouTube after a long break.
claims: The low-rep method claims 4-6 or 4-8 reps is superior for hypertrophy and anything above 8 reps is junk volume
He found Paul Carter polite in private despite his reputation, and his views of Carter don't color his analysis
A good hypertrophy method allows steady progression, doesn't cause injury and isn't too hard to recover from
5x5 gives fast early progress but then plateaus hard, so it is a poor hypertrophy scheme
Never use static rep targets; past the beginner phase progression mostly comes from adding reps within a range
Low reps like 4 on a cable lateral raise are impractical: too close to your 1RM and clunky
Low rep ranges work well for compounds and weighted calisthenics like weighted dips, where 8-12 is brutal and progress slow
On hard-to-progress isolation like incline curls, 8 reps at 40 lb won't turn into 4 reps with the next jump; 6-10 lets you add the weight
In 4-8 the bottom is 50% of the top while in 6-10 it is 60%, so each rep added in a wider higher range is easier and progression smoother
4-6 gives only two reps of room before a weight jump, a recipe for plateaus
Progressing on 4-6 while keeping reps in reserve is just sandbagging, which defeats the high-intensity premise
He proposes fatigue roughly equals reps times weight, modulated by the lift: 10-15 reps at 50 lb is a lot for laterals and nothing for good mornings
The stronger you get, the less recovery keeps up with strength; he needs about 72 hours to recover from hard lower-body work
After two sets of 8-12 Bulgarian split squats on Monday he was still sore on Friday, so lower reps might fit very taxing lifts
To cut fatigue you can do fewer sets instead of fewer reps; two sets per taxing lift works very well as long as you progress
Volume only serves the purpose of progression
Two sets of 8-12 and three sets of 4-8 save similar total reps, so fatigue depends on overall volume, not rep count
Fatigue management matters, but stimulus and fatigue cannot be separated: every set produces both
Recovery pot analogy: volume fills the pot, recovery evaporates fatigue and keeps stimulus; junk volume brings lots of fatigue for little stimulus
Quality volume is volume very close to failure; he disagrees that around 65% effort is enough
You can reach true failure at 12 or 15 reps; brief recovery between reps in a long set does not make it fake failure
Higher reps are more forgiving and let you grind; with 4-8 on incline dumbbell press slowing at rep 5 means no rep 6, while in 8-12 you can grind from 8 to 12
If you plateau in a range, adjust the range to fit the exercise; widen it if low reps stall, shrink it if high reps stall
Rest-pause works best with higher reps: after 8 reps and 15 s rest you'll get about 4 more, but on a 3-5 set you barely get one
Run low-rep sets as straight sets with long rests; higher-rep sets can use rest-pause and shorter rests
Being bored during high-rep sets is a load-selection problem, not a rep-range problem
Most low-rep promoters train mainly on machines, because 4-8 to failure on free weights is hard on tendons
A methodology should structure your training, not limit it; he wants to use free weights, machines and cables alike
If a fringe theory denies what most agree on, like volume mattering, it is most likely wrong
The low-rep method is a softer repackaging of Mike Mentzer's HIT; it works mainly because it forces people who never trained hard to train hard
Switching from high to low reps makes strength shoot up short-term, but long-term progression is what matters
The idea of a special hypertrophy rep range is mostly dead; most ranges work if you train close to failure
He uses rep ranges between 3 and 15: 3-5, 4-8, 6-10, 8-12 and 10-15
Gimmicks are deliberately polarizing and contrarian to gain engagement
He was away for a long time because of coaching work (Score of Strategy) and now returns to regular uploads and streams
exercises: hard to progress; use 6-10 rather than 4-8
very fatiguing; consider lower reps or fewer sets
higher reps allow grinding closer to failure
